originalTitle: Aswath Damodaran warns against disclosure diarrhoea. Why the valuation guru wants Wall Street to end quarterly earnings
simplifiedContent: Aswath Damodaran, a well-known expert in valuing companies, thinks that companies are sharing too much information about their finances every quarter. He calls this "disclosure diarrhoea" and believes it leads to a focus on short-term gains rather than long-term success. Damodaran wants companies to only share important information, rather than flooding the market with too much data. This matters because it could change how companies report their finances and how investors make decisions. By focusing on more meaningful information, investors may be able to make better choices about which companies to invest in.

originalTitle: Market Focus: Meta's higher AI budget jolts shares, signals long-term push
simplifiedContent: Meta, the company that owns Facebook and Instagram, has decided to spend more money on artificial intelligence (AI). This news has caused a reaction in the stock market, affecting the price of Meta's shares. The increase in AI spending suggests that Meta is planning to focus on this area for the long term. This matters because it shows that Meta is committed to investing in new technologies, which could impact the company's future growth and profitability. As a result, investors are taking notice and adjusting their views on the company's potential.

originalTitle: US Stock Market: Arm Holdings tops Q2 forecasts on AI demand, shares fall on royalty growth concerns
simplifiedContent: Arm Holdings, a company that makes computer chips, did better than expected in the last quarter, earning more money than people thought it would. This is partly because many companies are buying its chips to use in artificial intelligence (AI) projects. Even though the company thinks it will continue to do well in the future, its stock price fell because it said it might not make as much money from smartphone sales as it had hoped. This is important because it shows that even when a company does well, there can be other factors that affect its stock price. The company's stock fell nearly 7% after it shared this news, which means investors are a bit concerned about its future growth.

originalTitle: Vedanta Oil and Gas share price fell 5.5% even after the Vedanta demerger firm turned profitable in Q1
simplifiedContent: Vedanta Oil and Gas, a company that was recently separated from its parent company Vedanta, made a profit of ₹945 crore in the first quarter of the financial year. This is a good sign because the company had a loss in the same period last year. Despite this positive news, the company's stock price fell by 5.5%. The company's revenue, which is the total amount of money it earned, increased by 8.5%, and its EBITDA, a measure of its profitability, rose by 61.2%. This drop in stock price is notable because it happened even though the company's financial performance improved significantly.

originalTitle: 1000% return in five years! Multibagger stock inches close to record high after Q1FY27 results
simplifiedContent: A company called Gokul Agro Resources has done very well on the stock market, with its stock price increasing by 1000% over the past five years. This means that if you had invested in the company five years ago, your investment would be 10 times bigger today. The company recently released its financial results for the first quarter of the financial year 2027, which seems to have made investors happy. As a result, the company's stock price has risen, with shares opening at ₹225.40 today, which is slightly higher than the previous day's closing price. This is significant because it shows that investors are confident in the company's performance and think it will continue to do well.

originalTitle: Stocks to buy for long term: Ventura's Vinit Bolinjkar on Nifty's year-end target; 10 stock picks for up to 85% returns
simplifiedContent: Ventura's expert, Vinit Bolinjkar, has chosen 10 stocks that he thinks will do well over the next 1-2 years. These stocks are from different areas, including energy and technology, and could potentially bring big returns, up to 85%. This means that if you invest in these stocks, you could make a lot of money in the long run. Bolinjkar's picks are meant to help investors make informed decisions about where to put their money. By investing in these stocks, you could see significant gains over the next couple of years.
